title: How to Do Jumping Jacks Properly for Beginners
intro: Jumping jacks are a jump where you open and close your legs while raising your arms, and they get your heart rate up fast. There's a no-jump version for those just starting or living in a condo.
muscles: Calves, thighs, glutes, shoulders and tummy muscles. The main focus is heart and lung stamina.
steps: Stand tall, feet together and arms by your sides.
Do a small jump while opening your feet shoulder-width apart and raising your arms overhead.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, knees slightly bent.
Jump again to bring your feet together and lower your arms.
mistakes: Landing with straight, stiff knees. Bend your knees slightly to absorb the impact.
Knees caving inward when landing. Make sure your knees follow the direction of your toes.
Going so fast that your technique gets messy. Better moderate but correct.
easier: Step jack: step your right foot to the side while raising your arms, come back, then the left foot. No jumping, kinder to your joints and the neighbours below.
harder: Increase the speed, add more time per set, or do seal jacks (clap your hands in front of your chest).
dose: Beginner: 3 sets x 20-30 seconds, rest 30-60 seconds. Do it 2-3 times a week, can be part of a workout circuit.
safety: Wear shoes and make sure the floor isn't slippery. Stop if you have knee, ankle or chest pain, feel dizzy, or leak a little urine while jumping (common after giving birth), and get a doctor's or physio's opinion.

faq.q: I live in a condo and worry about noise. What can I do?
faq.a: Do step jacks without jumping. Your heart rate still goes up, but it's quieter and gentler on your joints.

faq.q: I just gave birth. Can I do jumping jacks?
faq.a: Start with the no-jump version first. Get your doctor's clearance before doing jumping exercises, especially if you have urine leakage or a heavy feeling down below.

faq.q: Are jumping jacks better than walking?
faq.a: Both are good. Jumping jacks are more intense in a short time, walking is easier to do every day. Pick the one you can do consistently.
